text:
deploy-bot: Rollout v2026.03.18-canary to eu-west-1 started. Running smoke set: prefix-prefill, warmup-heartbeat, embed-latency. Initial results: prefix-prefill reporting elevated 429s (0.9%) and warmup-heartbeat p95 increased 2x.

emily: seeing 429 spike correlating with prefill requests. dashboard shows queue depth on prefill worker pool spiking.

synth-watchdog: failing probes: 11/120 (9.2%) for prefix-prefill; 429s with body: "prefill-throttle". Host distribution: eu-w1-prefill-02..05, mostly under heavy load.

rishi: we turned on aggressive prefill when switching to lite-tokenizer to improve cold-starts. looks like the prefill workers aren't autoscaling fast enough.

ops-bot: auto-suggested mitigation: enable fallback routing for prefills to stable path and reduce canary to 2%. Command: `deploy-bot modify-rollout --model rwd-t5-lite --canary 2 --route-prefill stable`

emily: +1 to fallback. we want to preserve user-facing latency — better to route prefills to stable runtime until we fix autoscaler.

rishi: alternative is to increase prefill worker concurrency and add a short backoff on prefill failures. but that needs a quick patch and deploy. fallback routing is lower risk.

deploy-bot: Proposed action: A) apply fallback routing for prefill requests to rwd-t5-stable, B) reduce canary to 2%, C) mark rollout paused for prefill-affecting variants. Execute? (confirm with `yes`)

emily: yes. execute.
deploy-bot: Executing: `deploy-bot modify-rollout --model rwd-t5-lite --canary 2 --route-prefill rwd-t5-stable --note "temporary prefill fallback due to prefill worker queue spike"`

synth-watchdog: Scheduling targeted recheck in 90s. Will monitor prefix-prefill 429 rate and warmup-heartbeat p95.

(90s later)
synth-watchdog: recheck: prefix-prefill failures down to 0/120; global 429s for prefill now 0.12%. warmup-heartbeat p95 reduced but still elevated (1.1x baseline).

emily: good. Can we keep the canary at 2% for now while rishi pushes an autoscaler tweak? If autoscaler is tuned we can re-increase.

rishi: I'll prepare a quick autoscaler config: `prefill_workers: min: 2, max: 20, cpu_scale_target: 55, scale_cooldown: 15s` and a small runtime patch to add jittered backoff on prefill failure (100ms +-50ms). Planning to ship within the hour.

release-manager: note for release notes: "Canary for rwd-t5-lite temporarily adjusted: prefill traffic routed to stable runtime due to prefill worker queueing at low canary percentages. Canary reduced to 2%; autoscaler config being tuned. No customer-facing rollback required."

ops-bot: setting alert: `prefill_429 > 0.5% over 5m` will trigger an incident.

emily: remind me to add a postdeploy check to the smoke suite: run a prefill soak for 10 minutes at canary percent to catch autoscaler issues.

rishi: creating task RW-1438: prefill autoscaler tuning + jittered backoff + small load test matrix (canary percents 2,5,10 with prefill rates 1x,3x,5x). attaching initial logs.

synth-watchdog: monitoring; will log final status in 30m.

(20m later)
synth-watchdog: status update: prefills stable at 0.05% 429s; warmup p95 at 1.02x baseline. no further action required.

release-manager: closing decision: keep canary at 2% and route prefills to stable until RW-1438 completes and we validate autoscaler. I'll add a blurb to the release changelog and mark the rollout as "paused-prefill" for tracking.

emily: thanks. follow-ups: rishi to post results of autoscaler tests, perf team to verify warmup p95 trend after autoscaler change.

deploy-bot: Reminder: to resume normal prefill routing after fixes use `deploy-bot resume-rollout --model rwd-t5-lite --route-prefill default --canary 5`

rishi: will do. ping me if the alert fires.

ops-bot: incident threshold set. monitoring active. :mag:

emily: good teamwork, keeping the release alive while protecting customers.
